thread:
alex: Quick sync — we need a lightweight 1-pager + SDR soundbites for positioning vs managed cloud AI platforms and infra vendors. Goal: ship to sales by EOD Wed.
jamie: +1. Make it scannable — 3 claims, 3 proof points, 3 rebuttals. SDRs hate long reads. :thumbsup:
priya: Recommend focus: predictable unit economics, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and built-in graceful degradation/fallbacks. Short proof points only.
tom: Agree. Also add a 'when to escalate' flow for inbound leads (cost/latency/regulatory). We should route unusual compliance asks to AE before demo.
morgan: From field: need discovery one-liners. Examples: "How do you model tail-latency under peak load?" and "Who owns model rollbacks in your infra today?" Those open useful threads.
alex: Drafting quick copy here — paste feedback inline pls:
```
Claim 1: Predictable inference unit cost — not surprises at month-end.
Proof: Dedicated pools + intelligent batching + per-route cost insights.
Rebuttal: "Our current cloud plan scales automatically" -> Sure, but autoscale == variable spend. We provide predictable reserved capacity with burst controls and clear per-token math.

Claim 2: Consistent behavior across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
Proof: Single API + rollout controls + same observability.
Rebuttal: "We already self-host for isolation" -> Great — we support on-prem and VPC with the same control plane and eval tooling so teams don't maintain separate stacks.

Claim 3: Reliability-first serving with graceful fallbacks.
Proof: Policy routing + model variants + automatic fallback keeps apps online.
Rebuttal: "We can just retry/queue" -> Retries add latency; our routing and KV caching reduce tail latency without blind retry loops.
```
jamie: These look solid. Can we add a one-line bench: "Typical customer sees 20–40% lower per-token cost after adopting batching + caching" — careful to label as "typical" not guaranteed.
priya: Yes label it typical and include a short footnote: sample workloads with 1–2k req/sec and mix of chat/generation.
tom: Routing rules suggestion for SDR ops:
- Inbound mention of cost/ops/throughput -> tag #sales-inbound cost-track
- Anything mentioning SLA/compliance -> #ae-enterprise-queue
- Benchmarks or RFPs -> #field-research (attach eval request)
morgan: For quick SDR soundbites, something short for each scenario: 
- Cloud vendor lock concern: "Keep flexibility — same API across hosted/dedicated/private."
- Cost surprise: "Reserved capacity + per-route cost breakdown = predictable spend."
- Reliability concerns: "Fallback policies mean fewer outages and degraded responses, not silence."
alex: Love it. Two asks before I send to sales: 1) short visual (one fig) showing routing/fallback flow; 2) final sign-off on the bench sentence.
priya: I can mock the fig (simple boxes) and sign-off on the bench wording if we keep the "typical" qualifier + footnote.
jamie: I'll run a quick roleplay with an SDR tomorrow AM and report back. If no red flags, tell me where to pull the PDF.
ops-bot: Document published to drive: https://redwood.company/drive/marketing/field-cheatsheet-vs-managed-llm (auto-upload).
alex: Thanks all — I'll fold edits and post the final 1-pager in #sales-channel by 5pm. :rocket:
